title.en: Distinguish casual and regular salaried workers
Describe the status of workers in India

say.en: A cement-shop owner, a mason on daily wages and a bank clerk all work. How do they differ in the way they earn? In this lesson: Distinguish self-employed and hired workers.
Distinguish casual and regular salaried workers.
Describe the status of workers in India.

body.en: Workers who own and operate an enterprise to earn their livelihood are self-employed, like the owner of a cement shop. Those who work for others and receive wages or salaries are *hired workers*. Hired workers who are not hired on a regular or permanent basis and get no social security are casual wage labourers, like construction workers. Those engaged on a regular basis, who get a salary and social security benefits, are regular salaried employees.

points.en: Casual wage labourers: short-term, no social security
Regular salaried: permanent, with social security

narration.en: A self-employed worker owns and runs the enterprise. Hired workers work for someone else: casual wage labourers have no permanent job or social security, while regular salaried employees have a regular job with benefits.
narration.kn: ಸ್ವಂತ ಉದ್ಯಮ ನಡೆಸುವವರು ಸ್ವಯಂ ಉದ್ಯೋಗಿಗಳು. ಇತರರಿಗಾಗಿ ದುಡಿಯುವವರು ಕೂಲಿ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು: ಅನಿಯತ ಕೂಲಿ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರಿಗೆ ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ಭದ್ರತೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ನಿಯಮಿತ ವೇತನದಾರರಿಗೆ ಇದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Kinds of workers

narration.en: Let us sort workers into their groups on the board.

say.en: All workers fall into two groups: those who work for themselves and those who work for others.
A shop owner or a farmer on his own land is self-employed. Anyone working for someone else for a wage is a hired worker.
Hired workers are of two kinds: casual wage labourers, hired for short spells, and regular salaried employees.
Self-employment is the biggest group, more than half of all workers. Casual and regular workers make up the rest, roughly a quarter each.
Casual workers get no social security, while regular salaried employees get benefits like provident fund and paid leave.

body.en: Self-employment is the major source of livelihood in India for both men and women, accounting for more than half of the workforce. Casual wage labour and regular salaried employment each account for roughly a quarter. In rural areas self-employment and casual wage work dominate, while in urban areas a much larger share of *workers* are regular salaried employees, because urban jobs need more skills and literacy.

points.en: Urban: larger share of regular salaried jobs

problem.en: In a village survey of 400 workers, 228 are self-employed, 112 are casual wage labourers and the rest are regular salaried employees. Find the percentage share of each group.

answer.en: Self-employed 57%, casual 28%, regular salaried 15%: a typical rural pattern.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. In a village survey of 400 workers, 228 are self-employed, 112 are casual wage labourers and the rest are regular salaried employees. Find the percentage share of each group.

say.en: Let us work through this together. In a village survey of 400 workers, 228 are self-employed, 112 are casual wage labourers and the rest are regular salaried employees. Find the percentage share of each group.
Self-employed: 228 divided by 400 times 100 equals 57 per cent.
Casual wage labourers: 112 divided by 400 times 100 equals 28 per cent.
Regular salaried: 400 minus 228 minus 112 equals 60 workers; 60 divided by 400 times 100 equals 15 per cent.
Check: 57 plus 28 plus 15 equals 100 per cent.
So the answer is Self-employed 57 percent, casual 28 percent, regular salaried 15 percent: a typical rural pattern.
